First khutba

Praise be to Allah, the Great, the Creator, the Distributor of provisions and morals. We bear witness that there is no deity but Allah, the Just in His giving, and we bear witness that our Prophet Muhammad is the Seal of His Prophets. May Allah’s peace, blessings, and grace be upon him, his family, his companions, and all those who follow them in goodness until the Day of Judgment. 

To proceed: I enjoin you, O servants of Allah, and myself, to observe piety toward Allah. Allah the Exalted says:

﴿وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ إِنَّ اللَّهَ ‌عَلِيمٌ ‌بِذَاتِ ‌الصُّدُورِ﴾

 “And fear Allah. Indeed, Allah is Knowing of that within the breasts.” (Surah Al-Maidah: 7).

O believers, the soul always requires continuous care and purification from its ailments. Glad tidings to the one who refines their soul from its faults and cleanses it from what afflicts it. Allah Almighty says: ﴿قَدْ ‌أَفْلَحَ مَنْ زَكَّاهَا* وَقَدْ خَابَ مَنْ دَسَّاهَا﴾.

“He has succeeded who purifies it, and he has failed who corrupts it.”

Among the most dangerous ailments that afflict our souls is envy, which is the desire for the removal of blessings from others. This is different from admiration (ghibṭah), where one wishes for a similar state or blessing without desiring its removal from the other person.

Envy is entirely evil, entirely harmful, and entirely dangerous. It is a grave sin that consumes good deeds, drives its possessor to prohibited actions, severs relationships, sows’ hatred between those who love one another, and breeds animosity between those who share affection until it even separates a brother from his own brother. Have you not seen what envy did to the brothers of Yusuf (peace be upon him)? It led them to denounce their father’s actions, and to attempt to kill their brother. Allah Almighty says in Surah Yusuf: ﴿إِذْ قَالُوا لَيُوسُفُ وَأَخُوهُ أَحَبُّ إِلَى أَبِينَا مِنَّا وَنَحْنُ عُصْبَةٌ إِنَّ أَبَانَا لَفِي ضَلَالٍ مُبِينٍ* اقْتُلُوا يُوسُفَ أَوِ اطْرَحُوهُ أَرْضًا يَخْلُ لَكُمْ وَجْهُ أَبِيكُمْ وَتَكُونُوا مِنْ بَعْدِهِ قَوْمًا صَالِحِينَ﴾.

“When they said, ‘Yusuf and his brother are more beloved to our father than we are, while we are a clan. Indeed, our father is in clear error. Kill Yusuf or cast him out to another land; the face of your father will then be only for you, and you will be after that righteous people.’”

How ugly is envy as a trait! That is why Allah the Most High has commanded us to seek refuge from it and from envious people, saying:  ﴿وَمِنْ شَرِّ حَاسِدٍ إِذَا ‌حَسَدَ﴾

“And from the evil of an envier when he envies.”

 The Prophet ﷺ also forbade it, saying: «‌لَا ‌تَحَاسَدُوا». و «‌لَا ‌يَزَالُ ‌النَّاسُ ‌بِخَيْرٍ مَا لَمْ ‌يَتَحَاسَدُوا»

 “Do not envy one another.” (Sahih Muslim), and **“People will remain in goodness as long as they do not envy one another.”  Moreover, the wise, the scholars, and the pious have all warned against it.

Ibn Mas‘ud (may Allah be pleased with him) said: “Do not oppose the blessings of Allah.” He was asked, “Who would oppose the blessings of Allah?” He replied: ﴿‌يَحْسُدُونَ النَّاسَ عَلَى مَا آتَاهُمُ اللَّهُ مِنْ فَضْلِهِ﴾

“Those who envy others for what Allah has granted them out of His bounty.”

Such individuals are those who oppose Allah's blessings upon His servants, wishing for their removal from others

 Allah said about those envious people: ﴿‌أَشِحَّةً عَلَى الْخَيْرِ﴾

“Greedy and withholding of good” They forget all acts of kindness, belittle every favor, distort every beautiful thing, and distort every good deed. Their envious souls suffocate at the achievements of others, so they diminish the value of others’ successes and innovations. Through their envy, they deprive society of benefiting from the intellects of its sincere and loyal individuals. 

When they see blessings bestowed upon someone, they envy them. If a colleague receives a promotion, they resent them. If a friend excels, they abhor them.

So beware, O servants of Allah, of envy. For many blessings have been lost, opportunities disrupted, and families scattered because of the envy of those who eagerly aspire to what is in the hands of others.

O servants of Allah, one of the remedies for envy within a person’s soul is to have faith in Allah’s decree and destiny, and His justice in the distribution of sustenance. Be certain, O servant of Allah, in your Lord; when you see His blessings upon someone, pray for their increase and prosperity.

The Prophet ﷺ said: «إِذَا رَأَى أَحَدُكُمْ مِنْ أَخِيهِ مَا يُعْجِبُهُ، فَلْيَدْعُ لَهُ بِالْبَرَكَةِ».

 “If one of you sees something admirable in his brother, let him supplicate for blessings for him.” (Ibn Majah).

When you see successful people, strive as they have striven, and you will succeed as they have succeeded. Know that having a pure heart and a sincere attitude toward those blessed with favors helps treat and eliminate envy. Therefore, monitor yourself, love goodness for others, as this will perfect your faith and spread love and forgiveness within your community.   If feelings of jealousy or envy begin to creep into your soul, be honest with yourself and deal with your mistake by regretting and seeking forgiveness.

And remember the story of the brothers of Yusuf (Joseph), peace be upon him. After they wronged him in their youth, they acknowledged their mistake, repented to Allah for their sin, and sought forgiveness from their father. They said:

﴿يَا أَبَانَا اسْتَغْفِرْ لَنَا ذُنُوبَنَا إِنَّا كُنَّا خَاطِئِينَ﴾

 O our father, ask forgiveness for our sins; indeed, we have been wrongdoers. They also recognized Allah’s favour upon their brother and apologized to him, saying: ﴿تَاللَّهِ لَقَدْ آثَرَكَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْنَا وَإِنْ كُنَّا لَخَاطِئِينَ﴾

By Allah, indeed, Allah has preferred you over us, and we were indeed wrongdoers. So Allah forgave them and elevated their status.

 O Allah, purify our hearts, content us with what You have given us, and protect us in ourselves, our families, and our wealth. Make us among those who act according to Your command,

﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا أَطِيعُوا اللَّهَ وَأَطِيعُوا الرَّسُولَ وَأُولِي الْأَمْرِ مِنْكُمْ﴾.

I say these words, and I ask Allah for forgiveness for me and for you.

The Second Khutba

Praise be to Allah for His abundant blessings and great grace. Peace and blessings be upon the Seal of His Messengers, our Prophet Muhammad, and upon his family, companions, and those who follow his guidance.

As for what follows: O believers, indeed envy contradicts nobility of soul, good character, and complete faith. Reflect upon the words of your beloved Prophet ﷺ:  «لَا يُؤْمِنُ أَحَدُكُمْ، حَتَّى يُحِبَّ لِأَخِيهِ مَا يُحِبُّ لِنَفْسِهِ».

None of you truly believes until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself.  

 Beware of all forms of envy and reflect on its harmful consequences, for it is disastrous for the envious person and those around him. The envious person does not find peace in his life, nor does his mind find rest. He is in constant pain and continuous distress, troubled within himself and disturbing the tranquility of those around him. He occupies his mind with watching others, always distracted, with a troubled heart. He brings upon himself the harm he wishes for others, and﴿وَلَا يَحِيقُ الْمَكْرُ السَّيِّئُ إِلَّا بِأَهْلِهِ﴾.

 The evil plot does not encompass except its own people.

So, beware of envy, O servants of Allah, and be cautious of its causes. Do not boast about the blessings Allah has granted you, and do not display arrogance and pride in what He has bestowed upon you. Rather, use these blessings to thank your Lord and to show kindness to others. Have you not heard the words of the Messenger of Allah, ﷺ «إِنَّ ‌كُلَّ ‌ذِي ‌نِعْمَةٍ ‌مَحْسُودٌ».

 Indeed, every person with a blessing is envied.

And beware, beware of comparing yourselves to others, or thinking that their distinction is a belittling of your status. Have you not reflected upon the words of your Lord: ﴿وَلَا تَتَمَنَّوْا مَا فَضَّلَ اللَّهُ بِهِ بَعْضَكُمْ عَلَى بَعْضٍ﴾.

﴿وَاسْأَلُوا اللَّهَ مِنْ فَضْلِهِ﴾

 And do not wish for that by which Allah has made some of you exceed others. (Quran 4:32). And ask Allah of His bounty. (Quran 4:32). By doing so, you will be happy in this world and succeed in the Hereafter.

O Allah, send prayers and peace and blessings upon our master and prophet Muhammad, and upon his family, companions and followers. May Allah be pleased with Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman, Ali, and all the noble companions.

O Allah, purify our hearts from envy, and do not put in our heart’s hatred towards anyone, and protect us from the evil of every envious person. O Allah, make us believers in You, worshippers of You, repentant to You, far removed from envy and its causes, dutiful to our parents, and have mercy on them as they raised us when we were young, for You are the Most Merciful of the merciful.  

Our Lord, whatever good we ask of You, give us and more, for You are the Bestower. O Allah, perpetuate stability in our country, perfect well-being for us, expand our provisions, and bless us in our spouses and children. O Allah, grant success to the President of the State, Sheikh Mohammed bin Zayed, his deputies, and his brothers, the rulers of the Emirates, and his trusted Crown Prince, in what You love and are pleased with.

O Allah, have mercy on Sheikh Zayed, Sheikh Rashid, and the founding leaders, admit them into the spaciousness of Your Paradise.

O Allah, encompass the martyrs of our homeland with Your mercy and forgiveness.

O Allah, have mercy on the living and the deceased among the Muslims, both men and women.

 O Allah, grant us rainfall and do not make us among the despairing. O Allah, send us relief, O Allah, send us relief,

O Allah, send us relief. (Our Lord, give us good in this world and good in the Hereafter, and protect us from the punishment of the Fire)

(‌رَبَّنَا ‌آتِنَا فِي الدُّنْيَا حَسَنَةً وَفِي الْآخِرَةِ حَسَنَةً وَقِنَا عَذَابَ النَّارِ).

Servants of Allah: Remember Allah, the Great, the Majestic, and He will remember you. And thank Him for His blessings, and He will increase them for you. Establish prayer.
